evaluation_evidence: The study distinguishes indoor airborne-computer measurements from its outdoor deployment on five UAVs. The results specify different configurations and video resolutions where appropriate. [pp. 10–12, Fig. 12, §VIII.A–B and Fig. 13, OBSERVED]

workload_evidence: Evaluation uses source video at three resolutions and six CNNs grouped by size. A separate intermediate-data compression test uses a VGG16 trained on CIFAR-10. [p. 11, §VIII.A; p. 14, §VIII.E, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: A deliberate disconnection of one cluster head leads to rescheduling across surviving nodes. The response is observed in the task sequence and latency returns toward the prior level after reconnection. The scheduling paragraph does not establish an outdoor disconnection test. [pp. 7 and 10, §§IV.C and VII.B; p. 13, §VIII.C, Fig. 16(b) and Table IV, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The paper reports workload-specific latency, per-node compute and memory overhead, and scheduling measures. Table III gives exact host-testbed latency by model and node count. Fig. 13 separately reports the five-UAV setting. [pp. 11–13, §VIII.B–C, Table III, Figs. 13–16, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Individual CNN layers can be divided into subtasks and executed in parallel. Equation (14) uses N assigned UAVs per layer, and Eq. (15) assigns at most S layers per UAV. [PDF p. 3, III.A System Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The heterogeneous simulated UAV computing platforms are Raspberry Pi 3B+, Orange Pi Zero and Odroid; the workload is image classification. [PDF p. 6, IV-A, simulation settings, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The binary nonlinear program minimizes capture-to-inference-output latency, with UAV energy, memory, computation and per-layer and per-UAV assignment constraints. workload_evidence: Image classification/target recognition using AlexNet, ResNet152, and VGG-16; image dataset not named. [PDF p. 6, IV.A Simulation Settings, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]

accepted_outcome_description: The authors report EECIA running times similar to Random, Nearest and DistInference; OPT has the longest running time in the reported comparison. [PDF p. 6, IV-B, Fig. 3 discussion and Table II, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Per-layer allocation without early exit: each CNN layer j assigned to one UAV i via binary delta_t,r,i,j. [PDF p. 4, III.A System Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]

The proposed online approach uses PPO with penalties for constraint violations. The implementation uses PPO2/MlpPolicy with a two-layer, 64-neuron-per-layer MLP. [PDF p. 9, III.C.5 PPO Algorithm]
workload_evidence: The surveillance simulation tests three classification networks: LeNet, AlexNet and VGG16. [PDF p. 11, IV, simulation results and analysis, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]

[PDF p. 15, IV & V. CONCLUSION, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: The paper reports 96.45%, 91.23% and 82.50% constraint-satisfaction accuracy for LeNet, AlexNet and VGG16. In a separate policy comparison PPO achieved 94% versus actor–critic at 88%. At 20 LeNet requests, mean total latency was 5.22 s at the 560 profile and 10.68 s at the 256 profile. [PDF p. 12, IV. SIMULATION RESULTS, OBSERVED]

The rate distributions used in the evaluation include U[0,0.005] (Best) and U[0.1,0.5] (Poor). [PDF p. 3, II.A Reliability Model, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: The assigned unit is a configured video stream or chunk. UAVs sample and resize frames before upload. The edge performs detection on offloaded frames. [p. 4, §III; p. 10, §VI, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Simulations use car-mounted stereo footage as a controlled input and synthesize UAV positions and coverage. They distinguish a single-UAV runtime scenario from multi-UAV coverage tests. [pp. 10–12, §VI and Figs. 4–8, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: Joint stream selection, resolution and frame-rate choices maximize effective weighted surveillance coverage subject to accuracy, delay, bandwidth and edge compute constraints. The method combines a learned accuracy profiler and greedy local search. [pp. 5–6, §§III–IV; pp. 9–10, §V.C and Theorem 2]

mobility_evidence: Videos capture target/camera motion, while the multi-UAV scenarios assign surveillance positions and vary system conditions. The inspected experiments establish no evaluated UAV trajectory, handover or failure-recovery mechanism. [pp. 10–12, §VI and Figs. 5–8, NOT_REPORTED]
accepted_outcome_description: The report compares effective coverage and discusses how changing target dynamics affects detection accuracy and resource conditions. Coverage patterns depend on link bandwidth and compute capacity. It presents a bounded comparison to Random-to-upload for a particular bandwidth setting. [pp. 11–13, §VI and Figs. 6–8, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: The CNN is split into an input stage, two convolutional stages and an output stage. The stages run in separate containers and publish outputs to Redis. Docker Swarm orchestrates placement. [pp. 3–4, §§III.B and IV.A, IV.C, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Physical Docker Swarm testbed with two computer base-station stand-ins and two Raspberry Pi 5 UAV-node stand-ins. The setup and the test described in §V use physical electronics, with no live-flight condition established. Use body evidence in place of the inconsistent abstract device count. [pp. 4–5, §§IV.C and V.A; p. 5, Table II, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The implementation specifies container-placement constraints and recovery behavior. The inspected system model and implementation do not present a mathematical objective or an optimization solver for the evaluated system. [pp. 3–4, §§III.B and IV]
workload_evidence: The evaluation describes a TensorFlow CNN classifying aircraft images and a set of 100 images at 255 × 255 pixels. The test images are described as bundled in the input container. [pp. 3–4, §§III.B and IV.C; p. 5, §V.A and §V.B.1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: After deliberate disconnection of a device running a convolutional stage, the dependent stage waited and the input stage kept ingesting. Docker Swarm redeployed the container and it resumed from the last Redis checkpoint. No UAV motion was evaluated in this experiment. [pp. 5–6, §V.B.2, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The authors report per-stage time, classification accuracy and recovery after interruption. Fig. 3 labels four distinct stage timings. Their sum differs from the reported approximate end-to-end number. The paper does not establish how concurrent stage execution relates the two measures. Withhold the end-to-end number as a verified aggregate. [p. 5, Fig. 3 and §V.B.1–2, PARTIAL]

mechanism_evidence: The approach divides fused convolutional blocks into sub-blocks with overlapping spatial inputs. The scheme assigns the subtasks to matched server UAVs. [pp. 3–4, Fig. 2 and §III.A–B, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The paper reports simulations with common node power assumptions and a task-count sweep for the four benchmark models. Fig. 3 plots through 3,000 tasks. No physical flight experiment is described in the evaluation. [p. 5, §IV.A–B and Table I; p. 6, Fig. 3, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The formulation seeks to minimize total inference time. It bounds the number of servers per task and imposes a minimum transmission rate. Fine-grained partition and genetic-algorithm coalition matching are separate subproblems. Avoid substituting the coalition-fitness expression for the overall objective. [p. 3, §II.C Eq. (6); pp. 4–5, §III.A–B, Algorithm 1 and Eq. (11)]
workload_evidence: The simulated workload uses SeaShip images and four benchmark models, NiN, VGG16, AlexNet and ResNet18. Task arrivals are Poisson. The source establishes a visual workload with six ship types. Avoid an unqualified claim that an evaluated detector reports detection accuracy. [p. 5, §IV.A and Table I, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Bandwidth is held fixed in the network model. The inspected model and simulation do not establish movement trajectories, outages, migration or recovery tests. [p. 2, §II.A; pp. 5–6, §IV and Fig. 3, NOT_REPORTED]
accepted_outcome_description: DIA shows the lowest simulated total inference time on all four plotted model panels for the reported task-count sweep. Preserve the matched qualitative comparison. The abstract's range does not identify the exact model, task-count and comparator denominator needed for a verified numerical comparison. [pp. 5–6, §IV.B and Fig. 3, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Input/feature maps partitioned row-wise along height using Arbitrary Input Range (AIR) backtracking across conv/pool layers into N_m independent subtasks offloaded to UAVs. [PDF p. 3, II.C DNN Partitioning and Offloading, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The simulation distributes mobile devices across a square area and employs four clockwise-moving UAV edge servers at a fixed altitude with the base station at the centre. [PDF p. 6, IV-A, simulation setup, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: LaCPOO combines subgradient projection and CPOO; transmission powers are updated using KKT conditions. [PDF p. 6, III-C, joint optimization]

mobility_evidence: For failed return data under unreliable connections, the mobile device sends the whole task to the base station for reprocessing using maximum device transmission power. [PDF p. 3, II-C.2, Offload to BS, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: LaCPOO achieved the lowest average delay for most tested DNNs and reduced transmission power relative to CPOO in the model comparison. It had the lowest average delay in the plotted bandwidth sweep and lower average transmission power than the comparators in the reported offloading-reliability sweep. [PDF p. 7, IV.B Numerical Results, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: An integer partition variable sets local and UAV segments and allows either full offloading or all-local execution. [PDF p. 4, II-C, DNN Partitioning Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Python 3.7 and PyTorch 1.11.0 simulation with CVX solver; tested across 3 random seeds (2023, 2024, 2025). [PDF p. 9, IV.A Simulation Settings, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: A SAC policy with prioritized experience replay makes high-level decisions; a separate convex module solves UAV computing-resource allocation each slot. [PDF p. 6, III, proposed approach]
workload_evidence: Pretrained AlexNet, VGG16, and VGG13 models (VGG13 profiled in Fig. 1); dataset not named. [PDF p. 9, IV.A Simulation Settings, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: The method adjusts UAV trajectories through horizontal movement and altitude control. Task migration is triggered by remaining-energy or computational-load thresholds. [PDF p. 11, IV-B.3 and IV-C, trajectory and migration trigger, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: SAC+CVX is reported to converge faster and attain higher reward in the Fig. 4(a) comparison. It attains the lowest plotted average weighted energy in the user-count, UAV-count and resource-cap sweeps. Fig. 6 separately compares the four partitioning methods and shows that the proposed splitting strategy reduces weighted energy for the plotted algorithms. [PDF p. 10, IV.B.2 Performance Comparison, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Classifier-level DAG partitioning (enumerated partition points C) with offloading U_v,i^v' to neighboring UAVs. [PDF p. 7, V.B Algorithm, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Implemented in Python 3.8.19, PyTorch 2.3.0, OpenCV 3.2.0, CVXPY on Intel Core i7-13700KF CPU + 2x RTX 4090 24 GB GPUs using measured RPi 3B++NCS1/NCS2 latency/power. [PDF p. 9, VII. NUMERICAL RESULTS, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]

mobility_evidence: Table II assumes 200 m hovering altitude, 10 m minimum separation and 5 dB additional LoS attenuation. CONCLUSION, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

MAPDP performs well on latency, energy and throughput at larger sizes in the illustrated comparisons. For the separate 60-UAV efficiency sweep, Table III reports 0.511–0.515 s, 596.1–778.7 J and 116.6–117.4 IPS across efficiencies 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8. [PDF p. 12, Table III & VII.B, OBSERVED]

[PDF p. 3, Section II-B, Eq. (17), p. 3]

mechanism_evidence: The task-to-server decision is binary with at most one server per task. Local or deferred operation is described as a fallback. No split by model layer appears in the evaluated assignment variable. [pp. 5–6, §3.1; pp. 9–10, §4.1; p. 11, §4.2, OBSERVED]

decision_method_evidence: The formulation considers latency and accuracy with connection and compute constraints. workload_evidence: Complex model VGG16 and lightweight model AlexNet evaluated with top-5 accuracy for target tracking/recognition across multiple concurrent CNN streams. [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1, p. 8, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED] | The flight trajectories cite Mid-Air. mechanism_evidence: The architecture allocates portions of a pre-stored DNN to selected UAVs. It replans the unfinished portion when a selected UAV becomes unavailable. [PDF p. 4, Architecture Overview, p. 4, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: 4-UAV hardware prototype testbed with one NVIDIA Jetson Nano on UAV#1, one NVIDIA Jetson TX2, and two Jetson Nanos on UAV#2-UAV#4 with airborne communication modules. [PDF p. 5, Section EXPERIMENT SETUP, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: Uses a heuristic Observation-Orientation-Decision-Action (OODA) loop to sense swarm resources/topology, estimate latency, and adaptively update task partitioning. [PDF p. 4, Section ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW]
workload_evidence: Faster R-CNN object detection on a video stream (full DNN stored in advance on each UAV); specific video dataset name is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 5, Experiment Setup, p. 5, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Handles UAV unavailability by updating the partition strategy for remaining unfinished parts across available UAVs and recovers speed when the failed node reconnects. [PDF p. 6, Section EFFECT OF UAV UNAVAILABILITY, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: The prototype continued collaborative inference at approximately 2 FPS after one UAV became unavailable. mechanism_evidence: Decouples a 5 Hz strategic reasoning layer (70B target model at base station and 7B distilled draft model on edge via speculative decoding) from a 50 Hz execution layer via a Zero-Order Hold buffer. [PDF p. 5, Section 4.1 Cognitive synergetic hierarchical architecture, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The simulation uses JSBSim nonlinear six-DOF dynamics and the reported Python C-API wrapper, PyTorch 2.1/CUDA 12.1 and Ubuntu 22.04. decision_method_evidence: Formulates the multi-agent problem as a POMG and solves execution via Role-Decoupled MAPPO with GAT centralized critic, KL-divergence role regularization, and sequential intention propagation. [PDF p. 8, Section 4.6 Tactical execution layer]
workload_evidence: The strategic inference experiment uses a workstation-based DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B verifier (AWQ 4-bit) and Jetson-based DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B draft model (INT4). mobility_evidence: Evaluated under high delay/jitter (200 +/- 50 ms), Markov flapping links (2 s outage / 5 s in), AWGN (BER 10^-3), and up to 30% packet loss; includes ZOH buffer and Cognitive Fallback to Autonomous-Edge 7B/MAPPO mode on cloud disconnect. accepted_outcome_description: Table 4 reports mean win rates of 0.880 ± 0.02 in 2v2 and 0.790 ± 0.04 in 6v6 (SD), and Table 6 shows 0.74 for 8v8. mechanism_evidence: Each UAV executes the whole sampled task locally or sends it to one ground edge server. The formulation preserves temporal correlation across sampled frames. [p. 5, §3.3 and Eq. (19); p. 12, §6, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The analytical workload and channel run as simulations on an Ubuntu server. Baseline runs use a scenario with three UAVs, two fixed servers and fifty points of interest. Separate tests vary swarm size. [pp. 8–9, §5.1; p. 11, §5.2.5, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: MAPPO-HA trains a cooperative policy for 3D motion, frame sampling and binary offloading to minimize delay subject to sensing, accuracy and energy constraints. Its actor separates continuous and discrete action dimensions. [pp. 6–8, §§3.5, 4.1–4.2]
workload_evidence: The analytic workload models temporally correlated multi-frame recognition, with an accuracy function of sampled frame count and a compressed-model penalty. The setup uses 1080 × 1080 frames and allowed frame counts from 5 to 20 with gaps above 13. It reports no real-video experiment. [pp. 5–6, §§3.3–3.4; p. 8, §5.1; p. 12, §6, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: The model varies 3D trajectories and uses a minimum UAV separation. The discussion explicitly omits congestion-related loss and changing locations of mobile points of interest. The evaluated framework does not verify service recovery after node dropout. [p. 4, §3.1.1; pp. 9–11, Table 2 and §5.2; p. 12, §6, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The study compares modeled inference delay and accuracy and reports reward, sensing counts and fairness in particular experiments. The proposed approach shows lower simulated delay in the compared bandwidth sweep. This result uses the modeled accuracy function. [pp. 9–11, §§5.2.1–5.2.7, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Each UAV stores a replica of the trained CNN and executes assigned consecutive layers, forwarding intermediate outputs to the next UAV. [PDF p. 4, Section III-A UAV SWARM ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATION, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Custom simulation in Python 3.7.16 with TensorFlow 1.13.1 on Windows (Intel Core i7 / Xeon CPU 2.2 GHz, 4 cores, 16 GB RAM). [PDF p. 10, Section VI, p. 10, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: Jointly minimizes end-to-end latency and transmit power via iterative LDTP (Lagrange multipliers + CVX/Gurobi) and an online A3C-based multi-agent meta-RL solver. [PDF p. 8, Section V-B DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED META-RL SOLUTION]
workload_evidence: Evaluates image classification using two CNN architectures: 5-layer LeNet and 8-layer AlexNet on 32x32x3 RGB images. [PDF p. 10, Section VI-A SIMULATIONS SETUP, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Models dynamic UAV joining/leaving during learning (Fig. 7) and delegates tasks to another UAV while energy-depleted UAVs return to the central station. [PDF p. 6, Section IV Problem Formulation (Constraint C9), mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

[PDF p. 10, VI-B.1, Fig. 4(a)-(b), OBSERVED] | Across varying channel bandwidths, MARL-meta closely matches the theoretical sub-optimal LDTP benchmark in latency and transmit power while MARL-AC, MARL-DQN, and MARL-SAC exhibit higher latency and power usage. [PDF p. 11, VI-B.3, Fig. 6(a), OBSERVED] | Across Raspberry Pi 3B+ memory capacities (256 MB, 512 MB, 560 MB), MARL-meta delivers average total latency closest to LDTP and outperforms MARL-AC, MARL-DQN, and MARL-SAC. [PDF p. 12, VI-B.4, Fig. 6(b), OBSERVED] | Under dynamic UAV count changes (5 to 8 to 6 UAVs), MARL-meta adapts more efficiently with higher rewards and lower latency than MARL-AC, MARL-DQN, and MARL-SAC. mechanism_evidence: Single split point c_i(T_n) in {0..P_i} partitions the DNN into a local front part on RUAV_i and an offloaded tail part on SUAV_{o_i(T_n)}. [PDF p. 2, Section II-A Task Reception and DNN Partition Inference Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Each UAV holds a copy of the trained CNN and executes layers dynamically assigned by DRL-RLD based on memory, compute, position, and operability. [PDF p. 4, Section 2 System Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Evaluation uses simulation; Fig. 3 plots training reward through episode 1000. The inspected methods and experimental setup do not identify simulation software or host hardware. [PDF p. 9, Section 5.1, p. 9, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: Formulates end-to-end latency minimization as an ILP with binary layer-assignment, cell-occupancy, and operability variables, solved offline/online via PPO. [PDF p. 5, Section 3 Problem Formulation]

accepted_outcome_description: DRL-RLD achieves lower end-to-end latency than Layer-Avg, Comp-Avg, and Heuristic across AlexNet, YOLO, and VGG16 (Figs. 4-5) and maintains lower latency with minimal increase when 1 or 2 UAVs become inoperable (Fig. 6). workload_evidence: Llama-2 (7B, 13B, 70B in FP16) with causal KV cache processing simulated textual multi-modal UAV sensor logs (16, 32, 64, 128 tokens) for swarm coordination. [PDF p. 15, Section 4.1 and Table 1, pp. 15-16, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Evaluates robustness under +/-20% inter-UAV bandwidth fluctuation and Monte Carlo multiplicative Gaussian computation (10%/30%) and communication (20%/30%) noise. [PDF p. 21, Section 4.8 Robustness Analysis Under Environmental Uncertainty, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: At the Llama-2 70B scale (64-token input, 1000 Mb/s inter-UAV, 200 Mb/s air-to-ground), Edge-Solo and cloud-edge baselines (Cloud-Edge-Even, Cloud-Edge-Opt) failed with out-of-memory (OOM) errors. [PDF p. 17, 4.2. Latency on Llama-2 Models of Varying Scales, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: The offline alignment method assigns ranked teacher feature channels to student branches using device-capacity allocation and deterministic overlap. The master can select different exit depths for different assistants. [pp. 4–5, §III.C; pp. 6–8, §III.D and Algorithm 1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Hardware profiles feed a simulation with saved channel traces and separate validation/test roles. It is a profiled simulation of routing, with no full distributed on-device deployment reported. [pp. 8–10, §IV.A–B and Tables I–III; p. 13, §IV.E, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The sequential LinUCB exit router uses confidence and modeled computation, communication and synchronization costs, learns on the validation split and is frozen during testing. [pp. 6–8, §III.D and Algorithm 1; pp. 9–10, Tables II–III]
workload_evidence: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image classification with Wide Residual Network teachers and lighter multi-exit students. The experiment uses classification benchmarks in place of aerial imagery. [pp. 8–9, §IV.A and Table I; p. 13, §IV.E, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Time-varying link rates, bandwidth sweeps and assistant waiting are represented. The reported setup does not establish live mobility, a node-failure test or restart performance. [pp. 8–9, §IV.A; p. 11, §IV.C; p. 13, §IV.E, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: Under Table III conditions CIDER reduces routing-controlled computation and communication latency relative to Full Final Exit and reports lower accuracy than that comparator. The trade-off varies by comparator and dataset. The measured boundary excludes multiple sensing-to-output stages and overheads. [p. 10, Table III and §IV.B; p. 13, §IV.E, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: A node can forward raw inputs or already computed intermediate state to a neighbor, choosing a layer exit depth with respect to load. The method bounds redundant reconsideration. [pp. 2 and 5–8, Fig. 2 and §4, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The evaluation is software simulation with stochastic arrivals, mobility and heterogeneous nodes. It describes repeated independent runs, with no physical UAV test in the evaluation. [p. 8, §5 and Table 2, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The algorithm combines a diffused compute-capacity indicator, a threshold on offloading, and a congestion-aware early exit. Sensitivity to the threshold is evaluated separately. [pp. 5–8, §4 and Fig. 3]
workload_evidence: The simulator processes a modeled layered inference graph with two intermediate exits. The evaluation identifies an application example, with no named input dataset or specified neural-network implementation. [pp. 4 and 8, §3 and Table 2, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: Circular UAV trajectories and mostly line-of-sight connections drive modeled neighbor changes. Constraint and queue behavior mitigates redistribution loops. Physical node failure and recovery are not evaluated in the inspected simulation. [pp. 6 and 8, §§4 and 5, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The evaluation reports latency, outstanding work, transfer time, energy per task and fairness under scenario sweeps. Interpret early-exit results in the context of the model’s assumed exit accuracies. [pp. 8–12, §5, Table 2, performance figures and §6, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Cloud processing of uploaded features estimates confidence, then a per-UAV threshold selects cases requiring an additional quantized raw upload. [pp. 2–3, §II.A and Fig. 1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The edge–cloud experiment is simulated using synthesized data distributions. The cloud processing hardware is identified; there is no demonstrated flight test in this experiment. [p. 5, §IV.A, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The study uses per-UAV thresholds and raw-data quantization for accuracy maximization within a shared bandwidth limit, with alternating optimization. [pp. 2–5, §§II.B–III and Algorithm 1]
workload_evidence: CIFAR-10 test images are augmented to synthesize non-identical data across UAVs. ResNet-18/34 act as edge backbones and ResNet-101/152 act as cloud backbones. [p. 5, §IV.A, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: No UAV trajectory, outage or recovery evaluation is reported in the configuration or results. Spectral efficiency differences do not establish mobility validation. [pp. 2 and 5–6, §§II.A and IV, NOT_REPORTED]
accepted_outcome_description: The proposed policy reports higher top-1 accuracy across Table I model pairs and lower simulated end-to-end latency than Raw-Only. Its point-estimate latency is higher than GSUP and Feat-Only. [pp. 5–6, Table I and §IV.B, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Virtualizes worker UAV compute and deploys DNN partitions as containers managed by a per-UAV Container Manager using a heuristic placement algorithm. [PDF p. 3, Section 3.1.2 Deployment process, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Python implementation of Algorithm 1 and network/energy simulation; specific simulator package or host hardware is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 6, Section 3.6, p. 6, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: A MILP jointly accounts for normalized end-to-end delay and per-device energy consumption relative to available energy, under compute, memory, bandwidth, battery and placement constraints. Algorithm 1 greedily sorts candidate assignments. Reported complexity is O(|R||N|²) when the maximum number of partitions is fixed. Simulation weights are 0.9 and 0.1. [PDF p. 6, Section 3.5 and 3.6, pp. 5-6]
workload_evidence: The simulated search-and-rescue scenario includes concurrent AlexNet and VGG19 requests for object/person detection. The evaluation uses modeled inference profiles; the data availability statement says no data was used. [PDF p. 6, Section 4.1 and Data availability, pp. 6, 9, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Reference Point Group (RPG) 2-D mobility at fixed altitude z with 802.11s contention packet drop rate (PDR) and heterogeneous battery levels (halving battery on half of UAVs); node failure/recovery is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 4, Section 3.3 and 4.2, pp. 4, 7, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: In the 100 m² scenario, the authors report end-to-end latency advantages of up to 88% versus NN and HRE and 77% versus LO. Compared with NN, the authors report up to 90% less energy per device for homogeneous full-capacity batteries and up to 91% less when half the devices had half capacity. In the longevity simulation, the proposed method lasted 19 consecutive runs with 10 simultaneous requests per run on 10 UAVs. [PDF p. 7, Section 4.2 Simulation results, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Deploys a 10-layer head network with bottleneck early-exit on drones and full 32-layer model on aerial servers, supporting local exit, split upload, or direct offload. [PDF p. 5, Section 3.3 Model training, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: DNN built and trained in PyTorch; simulation averaged over 5,000 cycles per experiment; host hardware is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 8, Section 5, p. 8, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: Proposes two heuristic priority-queue upload policies (PLUTU and PLPTU) and an inverse-queue-length edge server load-balancing policy. [PDF p. 7, Section 4.1 Local processing policy]
workload_evidence: Branchy ResNet image classification model (32 total layers) trained and tested on CIFAR-10 (50,000 train, 10,000 test 32x32 RGB images). [PDF p. 5, Section 3.3 Model training, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]

accepted_outcome_description: PLPTU has the highest plotted system accuracy under limited wireless resources and in the shown task-generation sweep. The plotted system accuracy decreases for PLPTU and PLUTU as local compute declines, and their results converge at the lower tested capacity settings. No exact plot values are extracted here. [PDF p. 9, Section 5.1-5.3, Figs. 4-6, pp. 9-10, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Onboard inference tasks are assigned or reassigned across drones. The cited design is task-level allocation with local inference; no layer-level split is described in the relevant sections. [pp. 2–3, §§II.B and III.B, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The authors describe simulation with NS-3, ROS, Gazebo and MATLAB UAV Toolbox and a separate author-reported DJI/Raspberry Pi/Coral field prototype. [p. 4, §V.E, OBSERVED]

workload_evidence: The paper describes crop-pest detection, vegetation and soil monitoring, and yield prediction. It reports lightweight CNN edge benchmarking, but does not identify specific input datasets for those benchmarks. [pp. 4–5, §§IV and V.J, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: The design describes self-healing connectivity and redundant reassignment. Dropout and packet-loss results are reported, with no explicit link assigning the individual dropout comparison to the hardware field prototype. [pp. 3 and 5–6, §§II.D, III.B, V.F and V.K, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: Reported measures include decision and inference latency, energy and completion under load or dropout. Simulated and emulated conditions are explicitly named for some measures; modality is not assigned figure-by-figure. [pp. 5–6, §§V.F–L, Figs. 5–8, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Each task can pair its source with a selected neighbor and split a DNN at a candidate layer. The mini-batch pipeline overlaps communication and processing, with a local option. [pp. 5–8, §§III.D–E and IV, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: A custom Gymnasium simulator and a PyTorch/Stable-Baselines3 learner evaluate a set of common-seed episodes. Named hardware characteristics inform simulated compute profiles. [pp. 10–11, §V.A–C and Table IV, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The model uses a Pareto shortlist and DQN to jointly select the partner and partition under variable neighborhood availability and deadline/energy trade-offs. [pp. 6–9, §§III.G and IV]
workload_evidence: The workload uses image minibatches and profiled model configurations, including four networks in Table V and an additional transfer-analysis model. Named source image data are not reported in the setup. [pp. 5, 10, 13 and 14–15, §III.D, §V.A and Table V, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: The simulator models changing neighbors and link interruptions. The design includes assignment or local fallback handling. This is software evaluation rather than field-validated recovery. [pp. 3–4 and 11–12, §III.A, §III.C and §V.E–G, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: Under VGG-16 and VGG-19, the proposed method reports higher deadline satisfaction than the strongest same-substrate comparator. Local remains competitive on lighter workloads. Latency in Table V is end-to-end P50. [pp. 11–13, §V.D, §V.G and Table V, OBSERVED]
model_family_source_note: Original Table V, PDF p. 13, names YOLOv5m, VGG-16, VGG-19 and GoogLeNet-22.

mechanism_evidence: Selects N-1 ordered split points across L macro-blocks for pipeline parallelism, paired with a priority-aware cache replacement policy (weighting access frequency and loading latency) for 200 MB per-UAV caches. [PDF p. 4, Section 3.3 and 3.4, pp. 4-5, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Simulated on a Windows 11 (64-bit) server with 12th Gen Intel Core i5-12600KF, 32 GB RAM, and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 GPU; 20,000 PPO episodes (20 steps/episode). [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1, p. 8, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: Jointly optimizes discrete macro-block split points and continuous UAV displacement via PPO-DMCP, coupled with a frequency- and loading-latency-aware cache replacement policy. [PDF p. 6, Section 4.1 Problem decomposition]
workload_evidence: Models DNNs as 10-macro-block sequences and evaluates generalization across ResNet50, MobileNetV3, and BERT; focuses on latency rather than accuracy. [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1 Experimental environment and parameter settings, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: The model controls planar displacement with a 5 m minimum separation. A backup controller is described as a possible failover for the core UAV. The reported experiments do not include a failover evaluation. [PDF p. 8, Section 3.1 and 4.5, pp. 4, 8, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: At a maximum task completion time of 1.5 s, PPO-DMCP reached 100% completion and the lowest cumulative inference latency in the compared partitioning schemes. Figure 9(c) separately reports an average single-decision time of 31.9287 ms. [PDF p. 10, Section 5.4.2 and Fig. 9(b)-(c), OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: The architecture allocates sequential portions of a split neural workload across participating UAVs. [p. 4, §III.A and Fig. 2, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The authors report Python/PyTorch numerical simulation with a GPU for the study configuration. The evaluation is not a live or hardware testbed study. [p. 10, §V and Table II, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The study evaluates a learning-based coordination method with centralized training and decentralized execution. [pp. 7–9, §IV]
workload_evidence: The evaluation uses a layered neural network and software workload profiles. No underlying input dataset is identified in the inspected setup. [p. 10, §V and Table II, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: The software evaluation varies node participation and inspects the ability to continue inference after node losses. Hardware recovery is not demonstrated. [pp. 10–13, §V, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: The simulation reports task completion and inference-quality measures under alternative conditions. The findings are limited to the described software experiments. [pp. 11–13, §§V.B–D, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Inference uses distributed per-UAV representation extraction and task-guided collaborative fusion, with selectable semantic symbol granularity. [pp. 4 and 6–7, §III.B and §IV, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Simulation on an RTX workstation evaluates collaborative VQA under modeled communication settings. Table II characterizes candidate experts relative to onboard resources. [pp. 9–10, §VI.A and Table II, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: A two-stage learner jointly adjusts the UAV contribution weights and representation granularity toward task quality under a communication constraint. [pp. 7–9, §V]
workload_evidence: The study tests COCO-based visual question answering, identifies multiple edge expert backbones, and uses a task-specific semantic representation and codec. [pp. 6–7 and 9–10, §IV and §VI.A, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: The channel varies in the simulation. No explicit UAV trajectory, loss-based reassignment or recovery evaluation is reported in the inspected methods and results. [pp. 5 and 9–12, §III.C and §VI, NOT_REPORTED]
accepted_outcome_description: The study reports learning, task quality, granularity control and per-task accuracy. Comparisons against a single expert and controller ablations answer different questions. [pp. 10–12, §§VI.B–F and Figs. 5–9, OBSERVED]
model_family_source_note: Original PDF pp. 6 and 10 describe a Transformer codec and list CLIP-ViT-B/16.

mechanism_evidence: The method deploys redundant feed-forward shards offline and activates worker replicas selectively online. Leader-side state and worker-side aggregation have different roles. [pp. 4 and 7–9, §III.A and §IV, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: A discrete-event simulator tests fixed and stress conditions, with independent seeds and a shared timeout. The article explicitly leaves the physical prototype and on-device solver timing for future work. [pp. 9–10 and 14–15, §§IV.E, V.A and VI, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The optimization uses an offline placement phase and an online solver coordinating selective execution and communication under resource and reliability constraints. [pp. 6–9, §§III.E and IV]
workload_evidence: The simulator supports two FP16 Llama-2 sizes. Main displayed results use the 70B workload. The setup does not identify an empirical task or prompt dataset. [p. 9, §V.A, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: Worker redundancy, leader re-election and checkpoint recovery are described. Stress tests vary simulated network and mobility conditions. The paper leaves real-hardware recovery latency unmeasured. [pp. 9 and 13–14, §IV.E, §V.F and §VI, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The reported outcomes include completion, energy and latency. In the default 70B simulated comparison, latency is conditioned on success; reliability and latency therefore require separate interpretation. [pp. 9 and 11–13, §V.A, §V.C–D and Figs. 7 and 9, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Different UAV nodes host different expert components, and inference is assigned to suitable experts. An evaluation contrasts the expert assignment unit with layer-wise inference. [pp. 4, 6–8 and 12, §§III.C, V.B–D and Table V, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The study uses a software evaluation with multiple seeds and episodes. Physical validation is deferred by the authors. [pp. 9–10 and 17, §VI.A–B and §VII, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The method combines control and expert assignment under latency and communication constraints. A learned decision component is compared with alternative decision rules. [pp. 5–9, §§IV–V]
workload_evidence: The study models a mixture-of-experts inference workload with task and expert compatibility. The nominal simulator abstracts inference into inputs. The measured-gate subexperiment uses a CIFAR-100 classifier instantiation; this is not an airborne deployment. [pp. 4–5, 9–11 and 17, §§III.C–D, VI.A–B, measured-gate experiment and VII, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: Software evaluations vary network and mobility conditions, including disrupted connectivity. Some alternative conditions are sensitivity tests under the trained design rather than airborne recovery tests. [pp. 9 and 13–17, §§VI and VII, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: Completion, latency and resource use are reported in simulation. Interpret results by comparison table and operating condition; the review does not extend them to real flight. [pp. 9–16, §VI and Tables III–XII, OBSERVED]
model_family_source_note: Original PDF p. 11 contrasts MobileNetV3-Small expert and ResNet-50 monolithic classifier. MoE is the inference organization.

mechanism_evidence: The system divides input frames spatially with controlled overlap, performs worker-local inference and merges globally mapped detections. [p. 2, §§II.B–D, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Inference measurements use workstation processes with varying computational allocations to emulate UAV workers. The platform and video workload are stated in §III.D. [p. 3, §III.D, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The implementation assigns worker threads and frame regions and evaluates adaptive thread reallocation and heterogeneous allocation. The system is evaluated as a parallel implementation on a workstation. [pp. 2–4, §§II, III.D and IV.D–E]
workload_evidence: YOLO11m exported to ONNX evaluates urban surveillance video. The video content and resolution are described; the original video source is not identified in the inspected setup. [p. 3, §§III.B and III.D, PARTIAL]
mobility_evidence: The paper describes replacement of stateless workers and tests changing thread allocations on a workstation. It does not demonstrate interference, flight motion or real link-disconnection recovery. [pp. 3–5, §§III.C, IV.E and IV.G, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: Measured workstation outcomes include frame latency, throughput, detection quality and communication overhead; the evidence is specific to the emulated resource setup. [pp. 3–5, §§IV.B–G, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Per-task decisions select local or remote execution and model/input configurations. This is task-level allocation, with no consecutive-layer split. [pp. 5–7, §§III.C–D and IV, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The authors describe actual inference profile measurements and physical multi-UAV policy deployment, as well as offline training and modeled evaluation conditions. Modality depends on the reported result. [pp. 10–11, §VI.A and Tables II–IV, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: A multi-agent learner jointly addresses inference configuration and offloading and incorporates computation or transmission failures in the reliability model. [pp. 5–9, §§III.B, IV and V]
workload_evidence: Evaluation uses urban traffic video and object-detection CNN configurations at multiple resolutions. Request patterns are derived separately from an external usage distribution. [p. 10, §VI.A and Tables II–IV, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Evaluation accounts for compute and link reliability using modeled disturbances. The source distinguishes profiling and physical policy deployment from a simulated link; it does not establish an airborne outage experiment. [pp. 5 and 10–12, §III.B and §VI, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: The paper reports analytics accuracy and reliability-related outcomes. Measured model profiles in Tables II–IV are distinct from modeled system-level comparisons. [pp. 10–12, Tables II–IV and §§VI.B–C, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: Work is distributed between edge and cloud models at task level. Replay can revise prior inferences. [pp. 4–6 and 11–14, system model and §5, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: Experiments use a lab server and generated gridded simulation settings. Local and cloud labels are experimental roles. [pp. 14–15, §6.1, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The study describes generated fine-tuning samples, model selection and a scene memory/replay component for simulated edge–cloud coordination and model evaluation. [pp. 6–14, §§4–6.1]
workload_evidence: Fine-tuned language models process generated multi-UAV decision tasks. The evaluation uses separate training and test samples. [pp. 14–16, §§6.1–6.2, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Motion and decisions are simulated. Replay addresses inference errors; no actual network outage recovery validation is identified. [pp. 11–19, §§5 and 6, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The software results report task completion, processing time and system cost. Each comparison applies to its own workload and baseline group. [pp. 15–20, §§6.2–6.4 and §7, OBSERVED]

mechanism_evidence: A controller decomposes and updates shared tasks, using feedback from the agents. This is task-level sequencing and assignment rather than layer partition. [pp. 2–4, method and Fig. 3, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The authors identify workstation software experiments using Microsoft AirSim and comparisons implemented in MATLAB. Scene descriptions do not establish field flight. [pp. 4–5, §4 Experience and Fig. 4, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The paper presents a multi-agent policy variant and task-graph rules. It compares the planning component separately from scenario demonstrations. [pp. 2–5, method and §4]
workload_evidence: The evaluation includes multi-agent planning and perception-plus-planning scenarios in Microsoft AirSim. [pp. 3–5, method and §4, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: Simulated scenes vary obstacles and coordination. The inspected results do not describe a measured airborne outage or recovery test. [pp. 4–5, §4 and Fig. 4, PARTIAL]
accepted_outcome_description: The evaluation reports path length, planning-step time and success, plus separate plan-response time, task completion time and success for coordination experiments. [pp. 4–5 and 7, §4 and Tables 1–2, OBSERVED]
model_family_source_note: Original PDF pp. 3 and 5 identify Doubao-1.5-pro and Grounding DINO models in the evaluated framework.

mechanism_evidence: Handoff exchanges tracking state at task level. Matching and onboard tracking are separate from neural-layer partition. [pp. 4–5, §4.1 and §5, OBSERVED]
evaluation_evidence: The study compares trackers on recorded footage and reports hardware-in-the-loop operation including tracking, matching, coordination and navigation logic. [pp. 4–6, §5.1, Fig. 5 and §6, OBSERVED]
decision_method_evidence: The study describes tracker selection, feature matching, template padding and onboard implementation optimization. It tests configuration alternatives rather than an offloading optimizer. [pp. 3–6, method, §5 and Table 3]
workload_evidence: The tracker comparison uses a custom set of aerial marine footage, with changing views, partial occlusion and background noise. [pp. 3–4, dataset description and §5.1, OBSERVED]
mobility_evidence: The design addresses planned handoff of monitoring. Validation tests tracking and feature matching, and explicitly identifies the onboard system test as hardware-in-the-loop. [pp. 4–6, §4.1, §5 and §6, OBSERVED]
accepted_outcome_description: Results cover tracking accuracy, matching coverage and persistence, and onboard rate, power and compute behavior. Footage and HIL results support different claims. [pp. 4–6, §5 and Tables 2–3, OBSERVED]
model_family_source_note: Original PDF p. 2 describes the Transformer-based OSTrack model; §5.1 compares the trackers.
